profile.summary: HelixFold3 is the PaddleHelix team's open reimplementation of AlphaFold3. It takes a JSON description of the molecules in a complex, where proteins, DNA and RNA are given as sequences and ligands as a SMILES string or a Chemical Component Dictionary code, builds multiple sequence alignments with the usual search tools, and predicts one all-atom structure of the assembly. The output is a set of mmCIF files with confidence metrics, ranked by those metrics. Code and parameters are published for non-commercial use only.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: HelixFold3 follows AlphaFold3 as described in that paper rather than from released code, and is built in PaddlePaddle on the team's earlier HelixFold, HelixFold-Single, HelixFold-Multimer and HelixDock work. Prediction has two parts. First the pipeline searches genetic databases with jackhmmer, hhblits, hhsearch, nhmmer and hmmsearch to build alignments and finds structural templates up to a template date cutoff. Then the model runs, with a number of recycling passes and a diffusion module that samples several structures for the same input. By default each inference does 5 diffusion samples, and the report's own evaluation used 5 random seeds, 5 diffusion runs per seed and 200 sampling steps, keeping the predictions with the best confidence score.
sections.source_locator: README.md opening section, Running HelixFold for Inference and Resource Usage; technical report Section 1 and Section 2

quotes.text: Insights from the AlphaFold3 paper inform our approach and build on our prior work with [HelixFold](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.05477), [HelixFold-Single](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42256-023-00721-6), [HelixFold-Multimer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.10260), and [HelixDock](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.13913).

`kalign`, the [`HH-suite`](https://github.com/soedinglab/hh-suite) and `jackhmmer` are 
also needed to produce multiple sequence alignments.
In each inference, the model will infer `5` times (`diff_batch_size`) for the same input by default.

You can also
reduce the number of additional recycles by changing `model.num_recycle` in the same place.

Each sample is processed with 5 different random seeds, and diffusion inference is performed 5 times per seed with 200 sampling steps. The most accurate predictions are selected based on their confidence scores.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The first release accompanied a technical report dated August 2024, posted to arXiv on 30 August 2024 and last revised on 23 December 2024. The repository then announced HelixFold3.2 on 23 July 2025, reporting gains on protein tasks in FoldBench and fewer atomic clashes. The parameter file the README links is named HelixFold3-params-20250714.zip, so a result should name the parameter file as well as the repository commit. The README also states the environment it was validated in, Python 3.10, CUDA 12.0, cuDNN 8.4.0, NCCL 2.14.3 and Paddle 3.1.0, and says these settings are needed to reproduce the reported results. Output is not deterministic by default: the number of inference rounds, the diffusion batch size and the random seeds all change the structures produced.
sections.source_locator: README.md Updates, Environment, Usage and Running HelixFold for Inference; arXiv 2408.16975 abstract page dateline

quotes.text: 2025-07-23: **HelixFold3.2** brings significant advancements in protein-related tasks on FoldBench, along with a marked reduction in atomic clashes.
The parameters of HelixFold3 can be downloaded [here](https://paddlehelix.bd.bcebos.com/HelixFold3/params/HelixFold3-params-20250714.zip)
Specific environment settings are required to reproduce the results reported in this repo,

* Python: 3.10
* CUDA: 12.0
* CuDNN: 8.4.0
* NCCL: 2.14.3

sections.title: Licence and the hosted server
sections.body: This is not an open-source licence in the usual sense. The code, the parameters and their outputs may be used only by individuals and non-commercial organisations, or for journalism, and a commercial licence has to be negotiated with the authors. The terms also forbid building the code into unauthorised automated systems, naming screening and biomolecule design workflows as examples, and require derivative works to carry the same terms. There is a hosted alternative on the PaddleHelix website with an interactive interface and an API; the free tier of that server is restricted to non-commercial use and a paid tier allows commercial use.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Informed by the AlphaFold3 paper and implemented in PaddlePaddle, with recycling and a diffusion module whose sampling count and step count are configurable. The sources read do not describe the blocks or their widths.

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: A JSON file listing entities: protein, dna and rna given as sequences with a copy count, ligand given as a SMILES string or a CCD code, and ion. Residues can be replaced by a modified residue from the CCD. The pipeline also needs the genetic databases and a template mmCIF directory, since it builds alignments and searches templates itself.

run_guide.summary: Build the two conda environments, download the parameters and the reduced databases, then predict one demo structure on a single GPU.
prerequisites: The README's validated environment: Python 3.10, CUDA 12.0, cuDNN 8.4.0, NCCL 2.14.3 and Paddle 3.1.0.
A GPU with at least 32 GB of available memory, as the README suggests.
About 190 GB of download and 530 GB of disk for the reduced databases, plus aria2c to fetch them.
The alignment tools hmmer, kalign and HH-suite, installed by the msa_env step below.
Non-commercial use only: read the LICENSE before running this.

steps.title: Get the code at the pinned commit
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/PaddlePaddle/PaddleHelix.git
cd PaddleHelix
git checkout --detach 8e3991ab1209134b148b05d44e784a43eaa4484d
cd apps/protein_folding/helixfold3
steps.explanation: The README does not give a clone command. These lines are added to reach the helixfold3 directory at the commit this page was written from, which is what the README means by locating to that directory.

quotes.text: Locate to the directory of `helixfold3` then run:

steps.title: Create the alignment and inference environments
steps.shell:
# install msa env
conda create -n msa_env -c conda-forge python=3.9
conda install -c bioconda aria2 hmmer==3.3.2 kalign2==2.04 hhsuite==3.3.0 -n msa_env -y

# install paddlepaddle and other requirements
conda create -n helixfold -c conda-forge python=3.10
conda activate helixfold

python3 -m pip install paddlepaddle-gpu==3.1.0 -i https://www.paddlepaddle.org.cn/packages/stable/cu126/
python3 -m pip install -r requirements.txt
steps.explanation: Copied from the README. One environment holds the search tools, the other holds PaddlePaddle and the Python dependencies pinned in requirements.txt.

quotes.text:
conda create -n msa_env -c conda-forge python=3.9
conda install -c bioconda aria2 hmmer==3.3.2 kalign2==2.04 hhsuite==3.3.0 -n msa_env -y

python3 -m pip install paddlepaddle-gpu==3.1.0 -i https://www.paddlepaddle.org.cn/packages/stable/cu126/

steps.title: Download the parameters and the databases
steps.explanation: The README gives the parameter URL and says to place the checkpoint in ./init_models, and gives the database command as shown. The mkdir, curl and unzip lines are written here from that instruction; the README does not spell out a download command for the parameters.

quotes.text: please place the downloaded checkpoint in ```./init_models/ ```directory.
scripts/download_all_data.sh ./data reduced_dbs
The parameters of HelixFold3 can be downloaded [here](https://paddlehelix.bd.bcebos.com/HelixFold3/params/HelixFold3-params-20250714.zip)

steps.title: Run one prediction
steps.shell:
# edit run_infer.sh first: set PYTHON_BIN, ENV_BIN, DATA_DIR and --init_model
sh run_infer.sh
steps.explanation: The README's own command. It warns that the paths in the script must be set before running it: PYTHON_BIN to the python that has paddlepaddle-gpu, ENV_BIN to the environment holding hhblits and hmmsearch, DATA_DIR to the downloaded databases, and --init_model to the unzipped parameter file. The demo input it runs is data/demo_6zcy.json.

quotes.text: * Inference on single GPU (change the settings in script BEFORE you run it)
sh run_infer.sh
--input_json data/demo_6zcy.json
* Replace `PYTHON_BIN` with your python binary where `paddlepaddle-gpu` have been installed.

outputs: A directory named after the input JSON under ./output, holding one subdirectory per inference round and diffusion sample, each with predicted_structure.cif and all_results.json.
Ranked directories, demo_data-rank1 upwards, holding the same two files for the best predictions by metric.

notes: The context_length of 1200 in the structured row is a GPU memory limit on an A100-40G at bf16, not a model limit; the README gives 1000 tokens for a V100-32G at fp32. The record's entity level is a family, but the repository publishes one parameter file, HelixFold3-params-20250714.zip, and the README names two releases, HelixFold3 and HelixFold3.2, without saying which parameter file belongs to which; the structured row is therefore a single family row. The licence is a custom non-commercial Terms of Use Agreement, so no SPDX identifier is given on any source and store_bytes is false for the repository files. The technical report is a PDF, so the source saved and quoted is its text layer extracted with pdftotext, kept beside the PDF as artifacts/report.pdf. The record's two existing sources are the FoldBench benchmark paper and its supplement; neither was fetched, so no FoldBench numbers appear on this page.
